samples.summary: Many error envelopes bypass `outputError`, so they still emit multi-line pretty-printed JSON with no `command` — violating the newly-asserted §9 contract
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §9 (line 1017-1018) and packages/cli/README.md:116-118 both state errors are "a single JSON line on stderr" with shape `{"error":{"code":"…","message":"…","command":"docs.content"}}`. The diff only changes `outputError`, but a large set of failure paths hand-roll their own envelope with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and no command: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:126-137 (CONFIRMATION_REQ — the exact code README:120 promises), :164, :194, :201, :211, :245; packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:154, :194, :237, :244, :254, :312; packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:122, :159, :188, :197, :212; packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217, :227 (`errorJson` helper); packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:57; packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:195/:255/:307; packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:148/:203; packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:154/:204. A caller reading stderr with a line-delimited parser still breaks on these, and cannot attribute them.

samples.summary: `schema <unknown>` duplicates the error-envelope construction instead of reusing `outputError`, so it emits pretty-printed JSON without `command`
samples.evidence: schema.ts:32-39 builds `{ error: { code: 'NOT_FOUND', message } }` with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and sets `process.exitCode = 1` by hand — exactly what `outputError(new Error(...), this)` now does, including the single-line and `command` behaviour the diff introduces. The action already has `this: Command`, so reuse is one line.

samples.summary: `ctx` failure paths print bare text, not the JSON error envelope at all
samples.evidence: ctx.ts:61 `console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')` and :67 `Workspace not found: …` emit unstructured stderr, while docs/design/cli.md §8.1 promises "Errors are also JSON so agents can parse success and failure uniformly" and §8.4 lists `ctx.list`/`ctx.switch` as first-class schema commands. Pre-existing, but this change is precisely the one making error attribution uniform, so these sites are in the same lane. Same for packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:80/:63/:97.

samples.summary: `outputError` hardcodes exit code 1, so the §10 two-tier exit-code contract (2 for system/auth errors) can never be met through the envelope path
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §10 maps 401/403 and 5xx/network to exit 2 (and README:123-124 repeats it), but `outputError` unconditionally sets `process.exitCode = 1`. Not introduced by this diff, but the diff is the change that centralises envelope emission and would have been the natural place to close it.

finding.summary: Many error envelopes bypass `outputError`, so they still emit multi-line pretty-printed JSON with no `command` — violating the newly-asserted §9 contract
finding.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §9 (line 1017-1018) and packages/cli/README.md:116-118 both state errors are "a single JSON line on stderr" with shape `{"error":{"code":"…","message":"…","command":"docs.content"}}`. The diff only changes `outputError`, but a large set of failure paths hand-roll their own envelope with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and no command: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:126-137 (CONFIRMATION_REQ — the exact code README:120 promises), :164, :194, :201, :211, :245; packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:154, :194, :237, :244, :254, :312; packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:122, :159, :188, :197, :212; packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217, :227 (`errorJson` helper); packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:57; packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:195/:255/:307; packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:148/:203; packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:154/:204. A caller reading stderr with a line-delimited parser still breaks on these, and cannot attribute them.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds under direct inspection. `outputError` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:80-93) is the only shared envelope emitter and is the only thing made single-line/attributed. Every cited bypass site is real and reachable: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:126-137 emits the CONFIRMATION_REQ envelope via `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` with no `command`; likewise :164, :194, :199-205, :211, :243-249; packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:216-218 and its `errorJson` helper at :226-228 hard-code `null, 2`; packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:195 and :255 do `console.error(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2))`. I looked for an indirect normalization hop and found none — the `stderr` sinks are plain `console.error(line)` passthroughs (notes/import.ts:43-45, notes/content.ts:34-36, output/binary.ts:58-60). The contract is asserted at docs/design/cli.md:1017-1018 and packages/cli/README.md:116-122, and the README specifically names CONFIRMATION_REQ — the exact code emitted multi-line and unattributed. I considered refuting as out-of-scope on the strength of the scope note at docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:19-22 (deferring hand-rolled emitters to #654/#655), but that note is the change author's own task doc, #654/#655 appear nowhere else in the tree, and the acceptance criterion at :42 is stated unconditionally while the README hunk broadens the advertised contract. A user-facing contract the code does not honor on the path the README names is a spec-conformance gap in the design-fit lane, so the bar for refutation is not met.

finding.summary: `schema <unknown>` duplicates the error-envelope construction instead of reusing `outputError`, so it emits pretty-printed JSON without `command`
finding.evidence: schema.ts:32-39 builds `{ error: { code: 'NOT_FOUND', message } }` with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and sets `process.exitCode = 1` by hand — exactly what `outputError(new Error(...), this)` now does, including the single-line and `command` behaviour the diff introduces. verdict.reason: The quoted code is genuinely present — packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:31-41 hand-rolls {error:{code:'NOT_FOUND',message}} with JSON.stringify(..., null, 2) and sets process.exitCode = 1, and it does not import outputError (line 3 imports only `output`/`OutputFormat`). outputError in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:80-93 does now emit a single line with an optional `command`. However, the originating issue for this change explicitly carves schema.ts out: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:19-22 says "Scope note: this is the shape emitted when the shared envelope path is taken. Hand-rolled emitters that bypass `outputError` (... `schema.ts`) are the subject of #654/#655 and are left alone here." The plan section (lines 26-38) lists the call sites to convert — docs, slides, notes, cells, files, tabs, api-keys, sheets-import, sheets-export — and deliberately omits schema. The acceptance criteria (lines 42-46) are governed by that scope note. Under the design-fit/spec-conformance rubric, demanding schema.ts be converted in this diff is the unrequested scope creep this lens exists to prevent, not a failed acceptance criterion; the duplication is pre-existing and tracked under separate issues (#654/#655). Real, but not blocking under this lens.
